sentences.text:
Petitioner seeks for the following reliefs:
"(i) issue wit of mandamus or such other writ or direction or order directing the lst &
4th respondents not to insist production of original title deeds referred in Exhibit Pl agreement in Crime No. 812/2025 of Mayyil Police Station (ii) issue writ of mandamus or such other writ or direction directing the lst & 4th respondents to accept notarized copies of the title deeds referred in Exhibit Pl in lieu of the original deeds in possession of the petitioner."
2. I have heard the learned counsel for the petitioner as well as the learned Government Pleader.

sentences.text: 2 3. The reliefs sought for by the petitioner are primarily directed against the police to not to insist on the production of certain original title deeds in connection with Crime No.812 of 2025 of Mayyil Police Station.
The pleadings of the petitioner itself reveal that the aforementioned crime has been registered for the offences under Sections 420,465,471,468 r/w Section 34 of the IPC.
4. Obviously, forgery of a document is one of the offences WP(C) No.46814 of 2025 4 2026:KER:10358 alleged against the petitioner.
Though the counsel for the petitioner disputed the allegation of forgery, I am of the view that the requirements of investigation have to be identified and decided by the Investigating Officer.
Courts ought not to interfere by issuing directions as to whether any document is required or not.
Generally when forgery is alleged, original of the document becomes essential.

5. Apart from the above, the learned Government Pleader submitted that the petitioner is, in fact,
involved in 7 other crimes.

Taking into account the above circumstances, I am of the view that this is not a fit case where this Court can issue a direction to the Investigating Officer not to insist on the production of any document.
Accordingly, I find no merit in this writ petition, and it is dismissed.
